# import-boundaries (KIB002)

**Independent sibling packages**

This rule is enabled by default.

## What it does

Finds direct imports between local nested sibling packages so independent features do not depend on one another.

## Why is this bad?

Sibling features become difficult to change independently when they import each other's implementation instead of using neutral shared code.

## Options

Configured in `[tool.konform.lint.import-boundaries]`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source-roots` | `string list` | ["src", "."] | Python import roots relative to the config file. |
| `independent` | `string list` | [] | Optional module roots whose immediate child packages must remain independent. |
| `shared-package-names` | `string list` | [] | Sibling package names treated as neutral shared dependencies. |
| `allowed` | `boundary list` | [] | Reviewed importing/target prefix pairs exempt from both KIB rules. |
| `level` | `string` | "warning" | Violation level: warning or error. |

## Suppression

```python
x = 1  # noqa: KIB002
x = 1  # noqa: KIB  (every KIB* rule)
```
